rules.title: The Squad Cost Ratio system
rules.intro: From the 2026/27 season, the Premier League and the EFL Championship cap squad spending as a share of football revenue under the Squad Cost Ratio (SCR), replacing the old Profitability & Sustainability Rules. This page is 85Percent's plain-English summary of how the system works — the same logic the engine uses to compute your position.
rules.officialLink: Read the official Premier League statement
rules.refOnly: Reference only — not legal advice. Verify against the official 2026/27 Handbook.

s1.title: The core calculation
s1.lead: The Squad Cost Ratio measures total squad costs against football-related revenue:
s1.formula: SCR = Total Squad Costs ÷ Football-Related Revenue
s1.body: The compliance ceiling is 85% of revenue. The same formula applies in both the Premier League and the Championship — the Premier League adds three further solvency tests on top (see section 5).

s2.title: What counts as squad costs
includedItems: Transfer-fee amortisation (fee spread over the contract, capped at 5 years)
Player impairment (when book value is written down)
excludedItems: Assistant coaches and other coaching staff
Academy costs (but academy income still counts as revenue)
Women's team costs (but women's team income still counts)

s3.title: What counts as football-related revenue
left: Central league payments — merit, facility & solidarity
Domestic cup income (FA Cup, EFL Cup)
right: Net profit on player sales (fee minus book value)
Net profit from non-football stadium events

s4.title: The three zones, the allowance & the sanctions
s4.greenBody: Squad costs at or below <n>85%</n> of revenue — fully compliant.
s4.amberBody: Above the Green threshold but below the Red — a financial levy, no points deduction. The levy is the overspend multiplied by the percentage by which the ratio exceeds 85%.
s4.redBody: Above the Red threshold — a points deduction: a baseline of 6 points, plus a further point for every £6.5M spent above the Red line, imposed in the same season.
s4.allowanceBody: Each club starts with a <n>30%</n> allowance, setting the Red threshold at <n>85% + 30% = 115%</n> of revenue. Breach 85% at season end and next year's allowance shrinks by the size of the breach; stay compliant and it recovers by <n>10%</n> (up to the 30% cap). Unused capacity does not carry forward.

s5.title: Premier League solvency tests (SSR)
s5.intro: On top of the SCR, Premier League clubs must pass three Sustainability & Systemic Resilience tests. These don't trigger automatic points deductions — failing them brings monitoring, a required business plan and possible spending restrictions. (Championship clubs are not subject to SSR.)
s5.workingCapitalBody: Each month, cashflow plus qualifying funds must stay at or above <n>£12.5M</n>.
s5.liquidityBody: Liquid assets less liabilities must clear an <n>£85M</n> stress test (relegation, lost sponsor/broadcaster).

s6.title: Championship specifics
s6.ownerEquity: Owner equity top-up: up to £33M over a rolling three-year period (max £15M in a single season), which counts toward revenue for SCR.
s6.noSsr: No SSR tests — the three solvency tests are Premier League only.
s6.monitoring: Real-time monitoring by the EFL's Club Financial Reporting Unit.

s7.title: Assessment calendar
rows: Estimated revenues agreed → sets the season thresholds
Accounts Confirmation Test — actual vs estimated
SSR assessments — Working Capital, Liquidity, Positive Equity

rules.footer: This summary reflects 85Percent's reading of the published framework. The Premier League's own statement is the authoritative source.

nbv.ariaHow: How Net Book Value is calculated
nbv.title: How Net Book Value is Calculated:
nbv.body: The transfer fee you enter, amortised evenly over the contract length (capped at 5 years). Free signings and academy graduates carry £0.
nbv.formula: Formula: Initial Fee − (Annual Amortisation × Years Elapsed)
